plan.activation_condition: Observable when sampled P_O2 spans substantially below and above P50_O2 so that toe, mid-sigmoid, and plateau shoulder are all measured; especially in the cooperative transition regime around and across half-saturation.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: The same fixed-condition oxygen-equilibrium dataset shows the mechanism in training through mismatched toe/shoulder curvature relative to the parent, and the contrast extends in holdout when additional P_O2 points probe farther into low- and high-pressure regions.
plan.continuation_path: When the sequential binding constants collapse to an effectively geometric progression that yields a single cooperative shape, the Adair-style relation reduces closely to the parent Hill law over the sampled range.
plan.gap_statement: The parent assumes all cooperative binding can be summarized by one effective threshold and one global exponent, imposing a single sigmoidal shape that may be too restrictive for real equilibrium hemoglobin saturation curves.
plan.baseline_assumption: Relax the assumption that equilibrium cooperative loading is exactly represented by a one-step Hill approximation with one shared P50_O2 and one shared hill_coefficient.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Sequential oxygen binding to the four hemoglobin sites with unequal effective stepwise affinities produces equilibrium saturation curvature not fully captured by a single Hill exponent.
plan.rationale: Varied condition: oxygen partial pressure P_O2. Held fixed: temperature, acidity, carbon dioxide tension, hemoglobin concentration, and hemoglobin composition. The parent target mapping is a single-threshold Hill saturation curve, so after refitting one common P50_O2 and hill_coefficient it can only produce one symmetric cooperative transition shape. A scientifically natural refinement is to replace that idealized summary with explicit sequential equilibrium occupancy, which changes the target mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary trajectory. The observable contrast is curvature: under admissible measurements that span low to high P_O2, the child can show a flatter low-pressure toe and differently shaped shoulder near saturation while remaining monotone and bounded between zero and one. A single parent parameter set cannot generally reproduce both the toe and shoulder curvature of such a sequential-binding curve across the same fixed-condition dataset, because changing hill_coefficient and P50_O2 only rescales and steepens one common sigmoid rather than independently shaping multiple occupancy regimes. This refinement stays within the static equilibrium scenario and is only meaningful if the sampled P_O2 range actually covers the cooperative transition rather than an infinitesimal local region.

plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, varying P_O2 already reveals the sigmoidal loading law; with additional variation in P50_O2, holdout data show systematic horizontal displacement of that same curve family rather than a single universal threshold.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by holding P50_O2 constant across all samples.
plan.promotion_reason: A fixed P50_O2 hard-codes one affinity scale for the entire dataset, so the parent cannot represent admissible cross-sample horizontal shifts of the equilibrium saturation curve without separate refits; making P50_O2 an input is the minimal added freedom.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes one universal oxygen affinity scale for all sampled equilibrated blood conditions, excluding realistic sample-to-sample variation in the effective half-saturation pressure.
plan.baseline_assumption: P50_O2 is constant across all observations rather than an independently imposed or measured sample condition.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Effective hemoglobin oxygen affinity can differ between equilibrated samples, producing horizontal shifts of the oxygen dissociation curve while retaining the same cooperative binding structure at fixed composition within each sample.
plan.rationale: The parent already captures cooperative equilibrium loading versus oxygen partial pressure at fixed conditions, but it uses a single global threshold parameter P50_O2. A realistic next refinement is to relax that fixed-environment assumption and let P50_O2 vary across samples as an input summarizing admissible affinity differences. The varied conditions are P_O2 and the promoted P50_O2; the within-sample temperature, acidity, carbon dioxide tension, and hemoglobin composition remain fixed when each curve is interpreted, and the target remains the instantaneous equilibrium saturation itself. The concrete contrast is that two sample groups with different P50_O2 values have the same bounded monotone sigmoidal shape in reduced-pressure coordinates but are horizontally shifted in physical-pressure coordinates; at a common P_O2 near the order-unity range of P_O2/P50_O2, the lower-affinity group is measurably less saturated. A single parent parameter set with fixed P50_O2 cannot reproduce both groups simultaneously because changing hill_coefficient, adair_alpha2, or adair_alpha3 alters curvature and occupancy weighting but does not create independent sample-specific threshold shifts. This refinement changes the scored mapping from supplied observations to S_O2, not merely an auxiliary quantity. The limitation is that if all samples truly share one affinity scale, the promoted input is inactive and the parent is recovered exactly.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when sampled P_O2 spans at least the central transition region around P_O2/P50_O2 ~ 0.3 to 3 so that both early loading and late approach to saturation are measured; if all data lie only on one asymptote, the distinction is weak.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, mixed-affinity curvature appears as a broadened mid-saturation region; in holdout with wider P_O2 coverage, the same mechanism extends to a clearer low-pressure shoulder and delayed final saturation approach.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the two subpopulations have identical effective affinity scales or when one population's weight tends to zero.
plan.promotion_reason: A genuine mixed-population equilibrium requires one additional independently varying sample descriptor, such as the fraction of an altered-affinity hemoglobin subpopulation; existing inputs cannot distinguish compositionally different samples that share the same P_O2 and nominal P50_O2.
plan.gap_statement: The current law assumes every sample behaves as a single homogeneous hemoglobin population with one cooperative phase, omitting composition heterogeneity that can broaden the equilibrium oxygen dissociation curve even with fixed temperature, pH, and CO2.
plan.baseline_assumption: Hemoglobin composition is identical across samples and therefore all binding sites contribute to one homogeneous equilibrium binding polynomial.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Coexisting hemoglobin subpopulations with distinct effective oxygen affinities, such as differing fractions of variant or modified hemoglobin, produce a weighted superposition of saturations and therefore altered curvature of S_O2 versus P_O2 at equilibrium.
plan.rationale: The parent maps oxygen partial pressure to saturation through one cooperative transition after horizontal scaling by P50_O2. A realistic next refinement is to relax the homogeneous-composition assumption: across independently equilibrated samples, hemoglobin composition can vary, so two samples with the same P_O2 and similar nominal P50_O2 need not share the same mid-curve shape. Holding temperature, acidity, and carbon dioxide tension fixed, varying an added composition descriptor would change the curvature of the scored target itself, not merely an auxiliary quantity. The concrete contrast is that a mixed-affinity sample can load oxygen relatively strongly at low P_O2 because of a high-affinity fraction yet still require higher P_O2 for final approach to full saturation because of a lower-affinity fraction. One refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce that broadened crossover across composition conditions, because it has only one cooperative transition family per sample rather than a composition-dependent superposition. This effect is scientifically admissible when composition differs appreciably and measurements cover the transition region; if composition is truly fixed or the sampled P_O2 range is narrow and far from P50_O2, the refinement may not be identifiable.

plan.rationale: The parent already maps equilibrium saturation as a weighted sum of baseline and variant Adair-like binding curves, with P_O2 varied and temperature, acidity, and carbon dioxide held fixed. A realistic next refinement is to release carbon dioxide tension as an independently varied condition because hemoglobin oxygen loading is well known to depend on it even at equilibrium. This is a changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary interpretation: for the same P_O2 and hemoglobin_variant_fraction, the child predicts different S_O2 across carbon dioxide conditions. The concrete contrast is that higher carbon dioxide lowers effective affinity, so the saturation difference is largest around the transition region and small near both the zero-loading and high-pressure plateau limits. A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce that pattern across multiple imposed carbon dioxide tensions because the parent has no environmental input; it can only fit one common curve family over all such samples, or absorb one condition at the expense of another. The effect is scientifically admissible when carbon dioxide tension is intentionally varied while other within-sample conditions remain controlled or co-adjusted so monotone bounded saturation is preserved. If carbon dioxide is truly fixed experimentally, this mechanism cannot activate and the parent remains adequate.

response_change.parent_relation: S_O2 depends only on P_O2 and a sample-level variant mixture, so all curvature changes are attributed to hemoglobin subpopulation weighting and fixed cooperative parameters under one held environment.
response_change.child_relation: S_O2 depends on P_O2 and an added independently varied carbon dioxide tension that shifts effective affinity and can differentially modulate baseline and variant occupancy curves, creating a P_O2-by-environment interaction in the equilibrium saturation mapping.
response_change.observable_effect: At the same P_O2 and hemoglobin_variant_fraction, samples exposed to higher carbon dioxide tension show lower saturation mainly over the mid-loading range, with little separation near zero pressure and a compressed difference near the plateau.

diagnostic_groups.name: reduced_pressure_baseline
diagnostic_groups.role: baseline loading coordinate relative to the characteristic half-saturation scale

diagnostic_groups.name: variant_loading_coordinate
diagnostic_groups.role: variant-subpopulation loading coordinate relative to its affinity scale

diagnostic_groups.name: mixture_axis
diagnostic_groups.role: composition coordinate controlling how strongly subpopulation-specific environmental sensitivity is expressed

contract.activation_condition: Observable when equilibrated samples are compared across independently imposed carbon dioxide tensions large enough to shift effective affinity, especially for intermediate reduced pressures near the transition region; the effect is weak at very low P_O2 and vanishes as saturation approaches the bounded plateau.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, the mechanism appears as systematic mid-range horizontal/shape shifts across imposed environment values at fixed P_O2 and composition; in holdout, the same interaction extends to unseen combinations of P_O2 and variant fraction without changing the low- and high-pressure limits.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when carbon dioxide tension is fixed across all samples or when the new environment-coupling coefficient tends to zero, so effective affinity and cooperative shape no longer vary with that added condition.
contract.promotion_reason: The current contract holds acid-base and carbon dioxide conditions fixed, so no existing symbol can represent the known Bohr/carbamino environmental modulation. A new independently sampled static input is required to make that interaction observable in the scored equilibrium mapping rather than hidden inside refit constants.
contract.scientific_mechanism: Bohr/carbamino regulation alters hemoglobin allosteric balance and effective oxygen affinity at equilibrium, shifting oxygen loading differently across the pressure range and potentially differently for baseline versus variant hemoglobin fractions.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than retuning a coefficient because the effective reduced-pressure coordinates now depend jointly on P_O2 and the new environment input P_CO2, and differential baseline/variant sensitivity introduces composition-dependent environmental interaction rather than one globally fixed curve family.
contract.assumption_before: Carbon dioxide tension is constant and therefore has no explicit role in the saturation curve.
contract.assumption_after: Carbon dioxide tension is an independently varied equilibrium environment that shifts effective affinity, with potentially different sensitivity in baseline and variant hemoglobin branches.
contract.observable_signature: At fixed P_O2 and hemoglobin_variant_fraction, increasing P_CO2 lowers saturation predominantly through the transition region while leaving the near-zero and near-plateau limits almost unchanged; if variant_co2_affinity_shift differs from co2_affinity_shift, the P_CO2 effect changes systematically with mixture fraction.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this signature across multiple imposed P_CO2 values because the parent has no carbon-dioxide input at all, so it predicts identical S_O2 for samples sharing P_O2 and hemoglobin_variant_fraction regardless of environment. Refitting all existing parent parameters can fit at most one common compromise curve family over the pooled conditions, but cannot generate an explicit within-model P_O2-by-P_CO2 interaction with preserved low- and high-saturation limits across those same conditions.

range_suggestions.P_CO2: positive, experimentally varied across physiologic-to-elevated equilibrating carbon dioxide tensions
range_suggestions.co2_affinity_shift: nonnegative, small enough that 1 + co2_affinity_shift*P_CO2 stays positive over the sampled P_CO2 range
range_suggestions.variant_co2_affinity_shift: nonnegative, small enough that 1 + variant_co2_affinity_shift*P_CO2 stays positive over the sampled P_CO2 range
